With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. review_comments.body:
[NON-BLOCKING] Possible missing/undefined `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` in `UsernameForm`

The change updates `authenticate()` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { … }`, but this file/diff does not introduce a zero-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` in `UsernameForm`, nor is one obviously added in a shared superclass here. In contrast, `UsernamePasswordForm` defines `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This asymmetry suggests a potential compile error (unresolved method) or two divergent helpers. Please verify that `UsernameForm` (or an ancestor) actually defines a compatible no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`; otherwise either add it (or call the user-arg variant consistently) or centralize this helper to avoid signature drift.

[NON-BLOCKING] WebAuthn conditional UI now gated on `user != null` — potential regression for first-factor (no-identified-user) flows

Previously, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` executed when passkeys were enabled and the user was NOT already selected (enabling conditional UI for discoverable credentials on the username/password screen). The new logic moves the call outside the original block and gates it via `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which returns true only when `user != null`. This appears to suppress conditional UI setup for the anonymous/username-entry stage. Please confirm this is intentional and that initial-login paths without a preselected user continue to surface passkeys as designed. If it is intentional, consider documenting the behavioral change and ensure test coverage explicitly exercises the anonymous-first-login case.

[NON-BLOCKING] Conditional passkeys gating in `challenge(...)` now excludes anonymous-user error cases

`challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext context, String error, String field)` previously invoked `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. The new condition `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))` returns true only when `user != null`, so on error responses before user identification, conditional WebAuthn setup will not occur. If anonymous-first flows are meant to still display the passkey affordance on error, consider restoring a branch for `user == null` scenarios or adjusting `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(...)` semantics. If the change is intentional, please document it and ensure tests cover the anonymous-error path.

[NON-BLOCKING] Visibility change of `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` broadens API surface

The constant changed from `protected` to `public`. While this enables use from `AuthenticatorUtils` (via static import), it also exposes the symbol to broader consumers. Please also check for unintended external dependencies or binary compatibility implications.

golden_comments.comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] getForLogin returns unwrapped IdentityProviderModel instances on cache-hit paths, diverging from delegate path

In `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)`, when the cache is valid and `query` is present, the method builds a `Set<IdentityProviderModel>` by fetching each IDP by id and then returns `identityProviders.stream()` (see lines ~232-250). On the early-invalid or stale-id paths you return `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but on the normal cache-hit path there is no call to `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`.

This produces different shapes depending on cache state: sometimes callers receive organization-aware wrapped models, other times they receive the raw models. The follow-up change in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` to "re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped" hints at this inconsistency, but `isEnabled` is not the only potential behavioral difference. Returning a different model shape based on cache occupancy is a silent behavior change and will be extremely hard to reason about downstream.

Suggested fix: ensure the cache-hit return path maps each loaded `IdentityProviderModel` through `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (as the delegate path does), so that the model shape/semantics are consistent regardless of cache state.

[BLOCKING] Test added workaround (`isEnabled` re-check) masks inconsistency: returned models differ depending on cache state

The bean now does `filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && …) // re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped.` This compensates for `getForLogin` sometimes returning wrapped models and sometimes raw models. This is a symptom of a deeper issue introduced in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`: on cache-hit you return raw `IdentityProviderModel`s without the organization-aware wrapper. Callers should not need to defensively re-check `isEnabled` based on internal caching state.

Please make `getForLogin` consistently return organization-aware models (wrap in both delegate and cache-hit paths) and then drop this defensive filter from the bean to keep responsibilities clear and avoid subtle divergence across callers.

[BLOCKING] Inconsistent revision/counter usage when writing cache entries may break invalidation semantics

In `getForLogin`, the initial population path does `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, while the subsequent "searchKey not yet cached" path does `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. Mixing `startupRevision` and the live counter for the same cache key (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`) risks inconsistent revision tracking and invalidation behavior across nodes. At minimum it makes the revision embedded in `IdentityProviderListQuery` (`loaded`) diverge from the revision registered with the cache for the same logical entry. Use a single, consistent source of the revision/counter when adding revisioned entries on all paths.

[BLOCKING] Potential NPE when alias not found: `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` called with null

In `remove(String alias)`, you eagerly fetch `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` and then, when `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is true, you call `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)`. If the alias does not exist or the delegate returns `null`, `registerIDPInvalidation` will likely dereference fields (e.g., internal id) and NPE. Previously the code looked up the cached entry or used a non-null model; with this change, the null case is now reachable.

Guard against `null` before calling `registerIDPInvalidation`, or handle the null case by skipping the invalidation of the specific ID (you still invalidate the alias key and count separately) or by deriving the id from cache when available.

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pul.pr_title: Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations

golden_comments.comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] AuthzClientCryptoProvider registers as a CryptoProvider but most methods throw UnsupportedOperationException

`AuthzClientCryptoProvider` is registered via `META-INF/services` and will be selected whenever the default providers are absent (e.g., standalone authz-client usage). However, the majority of its methods (`getAlgorithmProvider`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getPemUtils`, `getOCSPProver`, `getIdentityExtractorProvider`, `createECParams`, `getKeyPairGen`, `getKeyFactory`, `getAesCbcCipher`, `getAesGcmCipher`, `getSecretKeyFact`, `getX509CertFactory`, `getCertStore`, `getCertPathBuilder`, `getSignature`, `wrapFactoryForTruststore`) currently throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (see e.g., lines ~73, ~80, ~87, ~94, ~101, ~138, ~145, ~152, ~159, ~166, ~173, ~181, ~188, ~195, ~202). Any code path in the client that relies on these capabilities will crash at runtime when this provider is selected. Given that `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` now explicitly calls `CryptoIntegration.init(...)`, this risk is not hypothetical. At minimum, these methods should delegate to the JCA defaults (e.g., `Signature.getInstance(...)`, `Cipher.getInstance(...)`) or the provider should not be auto-selected unless explicitly opted-in. As-is, this introduces a high regression risk for environments using only the authz-client artifact.

[BLOCKING] getBouncyCastleProvider returns an arbitrary JCA Provider (from default KeyStore), not a BouncyCastle provider

`getBouncyCastleProvider()` currently does:

```java
return KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider();
```

This returns whatever provider backs the default keystore type (often `SUN` or platform-specific), not BouncyCastle. Callers that request `getBouncyCastleProvider()` typically rely on BC-specific algorithms and will misbehave or fail subtly when handed a non-BC provider. If BC is not present, this should return `null` (and callers handle that) or explicitly load/return the intended provider; returning an unrelated provider is incorrect. Please either (a) return `null` when BC is not available for the authz-client use case, or (b) wire the actual BC provider when on the classpath.

[BLOCKING] Breaking SPI change: added abstract method `order()` to `CryptoProvider` without a default, breaking third-party providers

This PR adds a new method `int order()` to the public `CryptoProvider` interface. In Java, adding a non-default method to an interface is a binary-incompatible change: any third-party `CryptoProvider` (outside this repo) compiled against previous Keycloak versions will now throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when loaded via `ServiceLoader`, or fail to compile if they update. Given `CryptoProvider` is an SPI intended for pluggability, this is a high-risk breaking change. To preserve backward compatibility, `order()` should be declared as a `default` method with a conservative value (e.g., `default int order() { return 0; }`), or gated behind a new sub-interface. As-is, this must be accompanied by a documented migration note and version bump at minimum; ideally avoid breaking existing providers.

[BLOCKING] AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now performs global crypto initialization with the authz-client ClassLoader, which can have unintended side effects

The new line `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader());` introduces a global initialization side effect when any consumer calls `AuthzClient.create(...)`. This may override or interfere with a previously-initialized `CryptoIntegration` in the same JVM (e.g., application servers or libraries embedding both Keycloak server/client), and it constrains provider discovery to the authz-client's ClassLoader, potentially hiding app-provided providers. Factory methods are expected to be side-effect-free beyond creating the instance. Consider: (a) removing this implicit init and documenting that callers should initialize if needed; (b) scoping provider discovery to the call site without global state; or (c) only initializing when not already initialized and using the TCCL or caller-provided ClassLoader to avoid narrowing visibility.

[NON-BLOCKING] ASN1Decoder.readSequence does not handle indefinite-length BER (length == -1) and will silently return empty or partial results

`readLength()` explicitly returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding, but `readSequence()` assumes a definite positive `length` and loops while `length > 0`. If presented with an indefinite-length SEQUENCE (or a malformed input leading to `-1`), the method will skip the loop, returning an empty list without error. Given the caller (`asn1derToConcatenatedRS`) expects exactly two INTEGERs, it would be safer to either (a) reject indefinite-length encodings up front with a clear `IOException`, or (b) implement proper BER indefinite-length parsing. Since JCA ECDSA signatures are DER (definite length), rejecting `-1` is likely the simplest fix.

[NON-BLOCKING] Redundant/ineffective ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER

Inside `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, there are two lines:

```java
ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);
ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);
```

These create temporary encoders, write a value, and immediately drop the instances; they have no effect on the returned value and are likely leftover from development. Removing them avoids confusion and a tiny allocation overhead. The actual encoding is performed by the subsequent `writeDerSeq(ASN1Encoder.create().write(r...), ASN1Encoder.create().write(s...))` expression.

[NON-BLOCKING] Test asserts round-trip only; does not verify JCA accepts the DER produced from rs-concat or that conversions handle leading-zero/length edge cases exhaustively

`ECDSAAlgorithmTest` validates `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` -> `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` round-trip equality and a second round-trip, but it never verifies that the produced DER is accepted by `Signature#verify`, nor does it cover edge cases (e.g., values just over a power-of-two boundary that require leading zero padding, minimal-length INTEGER encoding, or negative `BigInteger` representations). Consider adding tests that: (a) feed the returned DER back to `Signature#verify`; (b) exercise R/S values with and without a high bit set to ensure correct zero-padding; and (c) test malformed inputs to confirm expected exceptions.

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pul.pr_title: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema

golden_comments.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] canManage() grants manage rights when caller only has VIEW permission on Groups (privilege escalation)

In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` the fallback path returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. This treats the mere presence of the `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type as sufficient to return `true` for `canManage()`. That is a privilege escalation: callers with `VIEW` on all-groups would now be reported as able to manage groups. The corresponding `canManage(GroupModel)` correctly requires `MANAGE` only. Fix by requiring only `MANAGE` (not `VIEW`) for the type-level check, e.g., `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`.

Evidence: `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java` — method `canManage()` added in this PR and uses `VIEW` in its predicate.

[BLOCKING] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns Resource IDs, not Group IDs — downstream filters likely expect GroupModel IDs

In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the set `granted` is populated with `groupResource.getId()`. This `id` is the Authorization `Resource` UUID, not the underlying `GroupModel`'s ID (which, per this PR, is used as the Resource NAME). Callers (e.g., `UsersResource.getUsersCount()` and `searchForUser()` now passing `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`) and `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` historically expect a set of actual group IDs. Returning resource IDs will cause filtering/counting to be incorrect or ineffective. Fix by adding the group identifier used for matching — e.g., use `groupResource.getName()` (which this PR sets to the `GroupModel` ID via `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`) when populating `granted`.

[BLOCKING] Contract rename `getGroupsWithViewPermission` → `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` not fully adopted across codebase (behavioral change)

This PR renames and changes the semantics from `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` returning a set of groups to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returning a set of IDs. Several call sites were updated (e.g., `UsersResource.getUsersCount`, `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`), but the interface removal of `getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel)` and renaming the bulk accessor creates a risk of missed callsites and behavior changes. At least one path still references the old per-group check indirectly (e.g., `UserPermissions.canViewByGroup` previously used `root.groups().getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)`, and was updated to `canViewMembers(group)`, which changes the effective permission from 'VIEW on group' to 'VIEW or MANAGE MEMBERS' on the group). This is a silent behavior change that needs to be documented and validated against spec. If the intent was parity with the old check, `canViewMembers` broadens access. Either:

- Restore a per-group predicate reflecting the old semantics, or
- Explicitly document and test the widened access scope, including potential regressions.

Evidence: interface at `services/.../GroupPermissionEvaluator.java` drops `getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel)` and `GroupPermissions.getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)` implementation is removed; `UserPermissions.canViewByGroup` now calls `root.groups().canViewMembers(group)`.

[NON-BLOCKING] Event listener registration now gated by feature flag at registration time — double-check that events during bootstrap are still observed when enabled at runtime

Previously, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` always registered a listener and internally checked `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` per event. This PR wraps the `manager.register(...)` call itself in the feature check, meaning no listener is registered unless the feature is already enabled at registration time. If the feature flag can be toggled at runtime after boot, events emitted before (or emitted when the flag is enabled but listener wasn't registered) would be missed. If the system does not support runtime toggling, this is harmless; otherwise it is an observability gap. Consider keeping the registration unconditional and checking the flag inside `onEvent`, or ensure registration happens after the profile is finalized. Evidence: change in `services/.../permissions/AdminPermissions.java` lines around the `registerListener` method.

[BLOCKING] Permission check widened: canViewMembers() now treats MANAGE_MEMBERS as sufficient to view members (semantic change)

`GroupPermissions.canViewMembers(GroupModel)` used to require `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` only. This PR changes it to `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)`, allowing holders of `MANAGE_MEMBERS` to also view members. That is a behavioral change that broadens read access. While it may be intentional, it is not documented in this PR and has system-wide implications (e.g., user listing visibility via group membership). If intended, add tests and documentation; if not, revert to requiring only `VIEW_MEMBERS`. Evidence: `services/.../permissions/GroupPermissions.java` modification in `canViewMembers` implementation.

golden_comments.comment: Incorrect method call for exit codes. The picocli.exit() method calls System.exit() directly, which is problematic:
Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Invalid call to `picocli.exit(...)` — `picocli` is a package, not a class; this will not compile

In `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()`, the new feature-flag guard calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);`. `picocli` is a package name and there is no static `exit` method on it; the correct pattern is to either `return` an exit code via the picocli command execution flow or call `System.exit(...)` explicitly. As written, this is a compile-time error. Please replace with an appropriate mechanism (e.g., `System.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` or return the code through the command framework) consistent with how other commands handle exit codes in this module.

[BLOCKING] Invalid call to `picocli.exit(...)` — `picocli` is a package, not a class; this will not compile

In `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`, the new feature-flag guard calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);`. `picocli` is a package name and does not expose a static `exit` method. This results in a compile-time error. Align with the command framework's existing exit-handling approach (e.g., return the code via the command runner or call `System.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`), consistent with other CLI commands in this module.

[NON-BLOCKING] Exit code re-mapping may break existing consumers expecting `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE == 4`

This change reassigns `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`. Any scripts, tests, or operators that currently rely on exit code `4` to mean "recreate required" will now misinterpret the result. Please audit call sites (shell scripts, operator logic, CI jobs) for dependencies on the old codes and either (a) keep `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` at `4` and choose a different code for `FEATURE_DISABLED`, or (b) update all consumers and document the breaking change prominently. At a minimum, add tests asserting the expected exit codes for both paths.

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pul.pr_title: Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema

golden_comments.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Behavior change: permission cleanup on role/client/group removal now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled

The listener in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` was wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java:~74-94). Previously, permission toggling on `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `GroupRemovedEvent` occurred unconditionally. This change silently stops disabling permissions on those events when the feature flag is off, which can leave stale permissions behind for non-FGAP deployments. If the intent was to gate only V2-specific behaviors, this guard is too broad. Please either justify this behavior change in the PR description and adjust callers, or scope the `if` block to only the V2 paths so legacy behavior remains intact.

[BLOCKING] Global-scope check does not ensure the Clients resource-type resource exists, leading to false negatives

In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String scope)`, the code does `resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId())` and immediately returns `false` when `resource == null`. By contrast, the per‑client variant `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` which auto-creates/returns the resource-type resource when missing and only returns false when no policies are attached. The discrepancy means global Clients permissions (e.g., `VIEW`, `MANAGE`, `CONFIGURE`) will not be recognized unless some other path has already materialized the resource-type resource in the store. Fix by mirroring the per-client path: obtain the resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` (and optionally short-circuit only when no policies exist), rather than failing on `null`.

[BLOCKING] Flaky test: assumes at least two default client scopes and indexes `get(1)` without checking size

In `testManageOnlyOneClient()`, after granting MANAGE for a single client, the test does `List<ClientScopeRepresentation> defaultClientScopes = clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes(); assertThat(defaultClientScopes, not(empty())); ClientScopeRepresentation clientScopeRep = defaultClientScopes.get(1);` (tests/.../PermissionClientTest.java). This assumes there are at least two default client scopes; on configurations with a single default scope this will throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException`, causing false negatives unrelated to the feature under test. Fix by asserting the size and selecting an element defensively (e.g., index 0) or creating/adding a second scope explicitly as part of the test setup.

[BLOCKING] `setPermissionsEnabled` (and other permission-management APIs) throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2 but are still invoked by core listeners

`ClientPermissionsV2` overrides multiple methods (`setPermissionsEnabled`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, etc.) to throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. However, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` still calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). With V2 active, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, so the listener will hit this UnsupportedOperationException at runtime when a client is removed. Either remove/guard the listener call when in V2, or provide a no-op/compatible implementation in `ClientPermissionsV2` that preserves prior cleanup semantics (or their V2 equivalent). As-is, client removal under FGAP V2 will fail with a 500.

[NON-BLOCKING] Unused import `AdminRoles` likely fails style checks

`ClientPermissionEvaluator` adds `import org.keycloak.models.AdminRoles;` but the interface does not reference it in code (only in Javadoc). Many modules enforce no-unused-imports; this can break the build. Either remove the import or reference the class in a type-safe way (e.g., use `@link` only without the import) if your style tool supports it. Also consider rephrasing Javadoc to avoid needing the import at all.

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pul.pr_title: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers

golden_comments.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Hardcoded provider ID string and missing null-check can cause NPE or wrong provider selection

`createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` looks up the credential provider using a hardcoded string: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`. This departs from the prior use of `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` (see removed import/usage in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction`) and risks a mismatch if the provider ID ever changes or differs from that literal. Additionally, there is no null-check on the returned provider; if `updateCredential(...)` returns `false` and the provider lookup returned `null`, the subsequent `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)` will throw a `NullPointerException`.

Fix:
- Replace the hardcoded literal with the factory constant `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` to keep IDs consistent.
- Add a null-check (and a clear error path) before invoking `createCredential(...)`, e.g., throw a meaningful `ModelException` when the provider cannot be resolved.

[BLOCKING] Security: raw recovery codes are serialized and sent to user storage without hashing/encryption

`createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` serializes `generatedCodes` to JSON and passes it as the `challengeResponse` in a `UserCredentialModel` to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. This results in the full set of plaintext recovery codes being written to the external user storage for providers that implement `updateCredential` and accept it. That both leaks sensitive secrets to a potentially less-trusted store and creates an inconsistency with the local-storage path (`credentialModel`) which (per existing provider contract) stores hashed/managed data.

Evidence:
- The method builds `recoveryCodesJson` from `generatedCodes` and constructs `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`.
- When `updateCredential(...)` returns `true`, the code logs success and DOES NOT invoke the local provider path which would create the canonical model.

Fix options:
- Do NOT send raw codes to user storage. [BLOCKING] Locale-suffix regex for building the English file path is unsafe on Windows paths and can overmatch across directory separators

In `verifySafeHtml()`, the English fallback path is derived via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. The character class `[a-zA-Z-_]` makes `-` a range between `Z` and `_`, which includes backslash (`\\`) and bracket characters. On Windows, this can overmatch through backslashes in the full absolute path, potentially consuming directory separators and producing an invalid `englishFile` path. This will throw at runtime (`new FileInputStream(englishFile)`) and break verification. [BLOCKING] Anchor sanitization mutates `value` while iterating with stale `Matcher`, leading to skipped checks and incorrect results

In `santizeAnchors(String key, String value, String englishValue)`, you obtain `Matcher matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)` and then mutate `value` inside the `while (matcher.find())` loop via `value = value.replaceFirst(...)`. This invalidates `matcher`'s internal state because it continues scanning the original string while `value` now points to a different string. As a result, subsequent iterations inspect stale content and may miss or misreport tags. Additionally, you're calling `replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` — removing the ENGLISH tag string from the TRANSLATION value — which only works if the tag strings are byte-identical (attribute order/whitespace differences will cause false negatives). Fixes:
- Compute against an immutable working copy (e.g., collect all translation anchor tags first, compare sets against anchors extracted from the English string), or rebuild the matcher from the updated string each iteration.
- Normalize and compare anchors structurally (e.g., parse and compare tag name + allowed attributes), not by raw string equality; at minimum, avoid mutating the string you're iterating over.

[BLOCKING] Anchor handling logic removes allowed anchors from the translation and does not enforce anchors required by the English source

`santizeAnchors()` strips matching `<a…>` tags out of the translation `value` (via `value = value.replaceFirst(...)`) before applying the sanitizer. The later equality check is then performed against this anchor-stripped `value`. Two problems:
- A translation that simply omits anchors present in English will pass verification (there is no check that every English anchor appears in the translation), which undermines the stated goal of ensuring safe-but-equivalent HTML.
- When English legitimately includes anchors, the verifier forces the translation to drop them to pass (since anchors are removed from `value` and `POLICY_SOME_HTML` does not allow `<a>` tags). This rejects perfectly valid, identical-anchor translations and accepts anchor-dropping ones — the opposite of the intended constraint.
Suggested fix: compare the multiset of `<a>` tags between English and translation (normalized for attribute order/whitespace), fail when translation has any extra or is missing any required from English, but do NOT mutate `value` before sanitization; instead, allow `<a>` in the policy only when the English text contains anchors and enforce exact-match on their attributes.

In `verifySafeHtml()`, after applying the OWASP `PolicyFactory` you do:

```java
String sanitized = policy.sanitize(value);
sanitized = org.apache.commons.text.StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(sanitized);
```

For disallowed HTML, the sanitizer encodes tags as entities (e.g., `<b>` → `<b>`). Unescaping immediately converts them back into literal tags, so `sanitized` may equal the original unsafe `value`, and your equality check `if (!Objects.equals(sanitized, value))` will NOT trigger — unsafe HTML silently passes. This defeats the entire purpose of sanitization. The comment mentions quotes and numeric tags like `"<1>"`, but this blanket unescape reintroduces all escaped tags.

Fix: compare against the sanitizer's output without unescaping, or selectively unescape only the specific constructs that are known-safe and required for i18n placeholders (e.g., numeric placeholders) — never general HTML tags. Alternatively, pre-normalize placeholders before sanitization and then compare the sanitized (still-escaped) output to a similarly normalized expected value.

`POLICY_SOME_HTML` only allows `br`, `p`, `strong`, and `b` with no attributes. However, existing message bundles (email/login) routinely include `<i>`, `<em>`, `<ul>/<ol>/<li>`, `<span>`, and `<a href>` with attributes like `target`, `rel`, and sometimes `dir` or `style` for RTL. Your code special-cases only anchors (by stripping them) and later strips inline styles for emails with `replaceAll(Pattern.quote(" style=\"direction: rtl;\""), "")`. This ad-hoc normalization will:
- Flag legitimate, non-anchor inline tags as illegal even when English source permits HTML.
- Remove only one very specific style while disallowing other benign attributes (e.g., `dir="rtl"`), breaking RTL rendering.
Recommendation: derive `POLICY_SOME_HTML` from an allowlist aligned with actual usage (e.g., OWASP `Sanitizers.FORMATTING.and(Sanitizers.LINKS)`), and allow specific attributes (`href`, `rel`, `target`) on `<a>`, and `dir` on containers when present in English.   .map((q) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters))
  .filter((q) => !q.hide)
  .filter((q) => q.expr);

golden_comments.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

review_comments.body:
[NON-BLOCKING] Global cache guarded by a package-level RWMutex — consider encapsulation to avoid global state

The new `entryPointAssetsCacheMu` and `entryPointAssetsCache` are package-level globals. While this fixes the data race, it cements global mutable state (acknowledged by the `// TODO: get rid of global state`). Consider encapsulating the cache behind a type (e.g., a small struct with methods) and passing an instance via dependency injection. This reduces hidden coupling, eases testing, and avoids future footguns where other code might read/update the same global without the mutex.

[NON-BLOCKING] Missing second cache check after acquiring the write lock (TOCTTOU window)

You `RLock`/read `entryPointAssetsCache`, `RUnlock`, then (on a miss) `Lock` and `defer Unlock`. Between the `RUnlock` and `Lock`, another goroutine can populate the cache. Without a second check under the write lock, this goroutine will still proceed as a 'miss' and recompute/overwrite the cache. This is a classic TOCTTOU gap. Please add a double-checked pattern: re-read `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring the write lock and early-return if it is now non-nil. Alternatively, use `sync.Once` (if the cache is immutable for the process lifetime) or compute outside the lock and only swap the pointer under the lock.

[BLOCKING] TOCTTOU gap: missing cache re-check after acquiring write lock can cause redundant recomputation and cache overwrite

You `RLock`/read into `ret`, `RUnlock`, then (on a miss or in `Dev`) acquire the write lock. Between releasing the read lock and acquiring the write lock, another goroutine can populate `entryPointAssetsCache`. Without a second check under the write lock, this goroutine will still treat it as a miss and proceed to recompute and overwrite the cache. Fix by double-checking after `Lock()`:

```go
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()
if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil {
    v := entryPointAssetsCache
    entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()
    return v, nil
}
// ... compute/populate
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()
```

Alternatively, restrict caching to non-Dev and use `sync.Once` for one-time initialization if appropriate, or compute outside the lock and only swap the pointer under the lock.

[NON-BLOCKING] Write lock is acquired unconditionally — including in Dev where caching is bypassed

After the initial `RLock`/read, the code takes `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` regardless of environment. In `setting.Dev` you don’t read from the cache and likely shouldn’t write to it either; holding the write lock around the (presumably) expensive asset computation will serialize concurrent requests in Dev unnecessarily. Consider moving the lock to only protect the minimal critical section where the cache pointer is (conditionally) updated in non-Dev, and avoid taking any lock at all in Dev mode.

golden_comments.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Coarse lock removal introduces race: duplicate/concurrent index builds for same key can corrupt or leak resources

`BuildIndex` previously held `b.cacheMu` for the whole method; this PR removes that and only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end (`pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:134-140`). Between method entry and the final cache write, multiple goroutines can now execute `bleve.New(...)` concurrently for the same `key` and call the builder, causing:

- Double creation/open of the same on-disk index directory (`dir`) with racy filesystem writes (corruption or transient errors).
- Two independent memory indexes for the same `key` with only the last one ending up in `b.cache`, leaking the other.
- Lost invariant that `BuildIndex` is single-writer per key during construction.

If the goal is finer-grained locking, the locking still needs to be at least per-`key` during build. Suggested fixes: introduce a per-key mutex (e.g., `singleflight.Group` or a `map[NamespacedResource]*sync.Mutex` guarded by `cacheMu`), or double-check `b.cache[key]` under lock before and after building to prevent duplicate builds. As written, concurrent callers can enter the build critical section simultaneously.

[BLOCKING] Init order change (search index before watcher) risks missing updates produced during initial index build

This PR reorders initialization inside `(*server).Init`: previously, the watcher was started before building the search index; now `s.search.init(ctx)` runs first and `s.initWatcher()` is started after (`pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:300-314`). This introduces a gap where writes occurring during the (potentially long) index build are not yet observed by the watcher. Unless `search.init` snapshots and then replays/merges changes from a monotonic source (e.g., using a consistent RV and then catching up), updates emitted during that window can be missed or applied out of order, leaving the index stale relative to storage. To preserve correctness while still avoiding lazy-init on first RPC, either:

- Start the watcher first and buffer/replay events with a high-watermark to be applied after the build completes; or
- Take a consistent snapshot RV for the build and then start the watcher with that RV to catch up deterministically.

As written, the window between build start and watcher start is unprotected and can cause lost events or inconsistent index state under concurrent writes.

[BLOCKING] Postgres integration test is blanket-skipped in CI, masking regressions introduced by this PR

This change introduces a permanent `t.Skip` for Postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a TODO comment stating it "Works locally" (`pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36-41` in the diff). Given this PR changes initialization timing and indexing semantics, skipping the Postgres path in Drone removes coverage exactly where concurrency/timing issues are most likely to appear. If Postgres is a supported backend, this skip needs a tracked issue and either a targeted flake guard (with retry) or a fix — not a blanket skip in CI. At minimum, restrict the skip to a known flake condition and file a reference issue; ideally, re-enable the test and address the root cause so this PR is validated against Postgres too.

`search.init` logs `duration_secs` as `end-start` where `end` and `start` are `Unix()` seconds (`pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:170-216`). For long builds this is fine, but for smaller namespaces and for latency SLO tracking, using `time.Since(startTime)` with millisecond precision (and the monotonic clock) avoids wall-clock jumps and provides actionable granularity. Similarly, the metric `IndexCreationTime.Observe(float64(end - start))` will benefit from sub-second precision.

golden_comments.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Ember computed property depends on `rejectedEmails.@each` but array contains primitives; changes won’t invalidate

The computed property that validates `accountEmail` was changed to `.property('accountEmail', 'rejectedEmails.@each')`. Using `@each` observes property changes on each element, which works for arrays of objects but NOT for arrays of primitives (strings). Since `rejectedEmails` stores strings, pushing a new email will not trigger recomputation. Use the array dependency key `'rejectedEmails.[]'` to observe additions/removals instead. Without this, previously rejected emails won’t invalidate the validator reliably after server responses.

[NON-BLOCKING] Case/whitespace sensitivity may cause client-side block bypass for same email

`rejectedEmails` stores the email returned from the server and checks `contains(email)` against the current input. This comparison is case-sensitive and whitespace-sensitive. Many systems normalize emails by trimming and lowercasing before validation; if the server also treats email case-insensitively, `"User@Example.com"` vs `"user@example.com"` or trailing spaces could bypass the client-side block. Consider normalizing both stored and input emails (e.g., `email.trim().toLowerCase()`) before pushing/checking.

[BLOCKING] Email matching is case/whitespace sensitive — blocked checks can be bypassed

`BlockedEmail.should_block?(email)` performs `where(email: email)` against the raw input. Without normalization, `"User@Example.com"` or emails with surrounding whitespace will not match a stored `"user@example.com"`, depending on DB collation. Neither `BlockedEmail` nor `EmailValidator` downcases/strips emails before lookup, and the migration does not enforce a normalized invariant. This allows client/server bypass of the block list. Fix by normalizing both at write and at check time (e.g., `before_validation { self.email = email.to_s.strip.downcase }` and call `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value.to_s.strip.downcase)`), and consider adding a functional index/constraint on the normalized value.

[BLOCKING] Silent behavior change: domain whitelist/blacklist moved to EmailValidator but no requires/autoload and no tests for User model’s behavior

The diff removes `User#email_validator` and `email_in_restriction_setting?`, replacing them with `validates :email, email: true`. This relies on `EmailValidator` in `lib/validators/email_validator.rb` being autoloaded. In Rails, custom validators must be under `app/validators` or explicitly required/added to autoload paths. Placing it in `lib/validators` without ensuring autoloading risks `ArgumentError: Unknown validator: 'EmailValidator'` or the validation silently not running in production where `lib` isn’t eager-loaded. There are specs for the validator itself but none that assert `User` runs it. Ensure autoload/eager_load is configured or move the validator under `app/validators`, and add/retain model-level tests asserting whitelist/blacklist still apply.

[BLOCKING] Validator performs database writes during validation via `BlockedEmail.should_block?`

`EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, and `should_block?` increments `match_count` and updates `last_match_at` with `save`. Validation callbacks are expected to be side-effect free and not perform writes; doing so introduces unexpected write load, potential deadlocks/validation recursion, and can raise exceptions that surface as 500s during a simple validation. If metrics are required, emit them outside the validation path (e.g., in a service after a failed `User#save`) or record them via an async job. At minimum, guard this behind a safe, non-raising path and remove the write from the validator.

https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua.pr_title: Enhance embed URL handling and validation system

golden_comments.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Dangerous default: sets cook_method to raw_html for all existing posts

`add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` assigns a default of `1`, while `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. This maps `1` to `:raw_html`, causing pre-existing and new defaulted posts to bypass the cooking/sanitization pipeline (`Post#cook` now returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`). This is a severe security regression enabling stored XSS across the site. Default should be the safe `:regular` (likely `0`), and a backfill/migration should ensure legacy rows are set accordingly.

[BLOCKING] ERB syntax error: uses `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`

The header block closes with `end if`, which is invalid ERB syntax and will raise a template error at render time. The block opened with `<%- if @topic_view.posts.present? %>` and should close with `<%- end %>`. See `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:1-7` — replace `end if` with `end`.

[BLOCKING] Raw HTML from feeds is imported and rendered without sanitization, enabling XSS

`poll_feed` builds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for this mode, bypassing Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. There is no scheme/attribute whitelist or sanitizer on the RSS path (unlike `import_remote`’s Readability tags/attrs). A malicious or compromised feed can inject `<script>`/`javascript:` URLs into posts viewable on the forum, a critical stored XSS risk.

[NON-BLOCKING] postMessage trust check is brittle and omits `e.source` validation

The origin check `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` is unusual and can be error-prone (it relies on `discourseUrl` containing the full `e.origin` string; ports/trailing slashes can cause false negatives). Also, you do not verify `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`, so any same-origin window on the page could send a spoofed resize. Consider strict equality on origins (normalize and compare) and assert `e.source === iframe.contentWindow` before acting.

[BLOCKING] Incorrect `postMessage` targetOrigin uses full referer URL, breaking delivery and weakening the origin contract

`parent.postMessage({…}, '<%= request.referer %>');` passes the full Referer (which includes path/query) as the `targetOrigin`. Per the HTML5 spec, `targetOrigin` must be an origin string like `'https://example.com'` (scheme + host + optional port). Supplying a full URL fails strict origin matching (message may be dropped) and couples the check to path changes. Compute and pass just the origin (e.g., `#{URI(request.referer).scheme}://#{URI(request.referer).host}#{port_if_non_default}`) or a fixed trusted origin derived from `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. This also aligns with the origin check in `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`.

[BLOCKING] `force: true` on `create_table :top_topics` will drop existing data on deploy

This migration was modified to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before creating it, which can delete production data if this migration is re-run in any environment where the table exists (e.g., schema drift, partial resets, or multiple branch deploys). This is a high-risk change to an existing migration and should be avoided; if a reset is intended, use a new migration with an explicit `drop_table` + `create_table` or adjust the schema without destructive defaults.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Unescaped HTML injection risk via triple-stash with user-provided title

The template renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (triple-stash) on line 3. The backing controller composes this string with `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`, where `model.fancyTitle` derives from the topic title. Rendering it unescaped allows any HTML in the title to be injected into the page, creating an XSS vector. Even if `fancyTitle` is usually sanitized, relying on it here with triple-stash widens risk. Fix by avoiding triple-stash and letting Handlebars escape (`{{stopNotificiationsText}}`) and/or by returning a SafeString that only wraps the `<strong>` tag while escaping the interpolated title (e.g., build the markup in the template with `{{i18n "topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications" title=model.fancyTitle}}` and single-stash, or escape `title` before marking safe).

[BLOCKING] State-changing GET endpoint without CSRF/auth token enables CSRF; also `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` removes an existing guard The new `unsubscribe` action (around `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:95-121`) mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` but is exposed via `GET` routes in `config/routes.rb` (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`, line ~438). There is no CSRF/auth token or signed link validation, and `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]` explicitly disables the XHR check for this action. A logged-in user can be forced to hit this URL (e.g., via an `` tag) and silently change their notification level — a classic CSRF. Fix by making this a non-idempotent verb (POST/PUT) protected by Rails authenticity token, or by requiring a time-limited, user-bound signed token in the unsubscribe URL and verifying it server-side before applying the change.

[BLOCKING] Route/template naming mismatch — route `topicUnsubscribe` will not render `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`

You declared `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` (camel-cased name). Ember’s convention maps that to the template `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs` and controller/view `topic-unsubscribe`. However, the template added is `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (nested under `topic/`), which corresponds to a nested route `topic.unsubscribe`, not `topicUnsubscribe`. As-is, navigating to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` will not pick up the intended template. Fix by either: (a) renaming the route to be nested under `topic` (e.g., define it within the `topic` resource as `this.route('unsubscribe', …)`), and keeping the template at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`; or (b) moving/renaming the template to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs` to match the flat `topicUnsubscribe` route name. Ensure the controller/view file names match whichever route you choose.

[BLOCKING] Possible `nil` dereference when `TopicUser` record is absent; also crashes for anonymous users

In `unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` assumes `current_user` and a corresponding `TopicUser` exist. For logged-out clicks (common from email) `current_user` is `nil` — calling `.id` will raise. Even when logged in, if a `TopicUser` row doesn’t exist yet, `tu` is `nil` and `tu.notification_level = …` will raise a `NoMethodError`. Guard for anonymous users (e.g., show a login flow or a confirmation page that doesn’t mutate state), and use `TopicUser.change` or `find_or_initialize_by` to safely set `notification_level`.

[BLOCKING] Email copy promises “stop receiving notifications” but server sets only `regular` level for tracked/watched topics

The added copy says: `To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url}).` However, the `unsubscribe` action (`app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-119`) sets `notification_level` to `regular` when it was previously `> regular` (i.e., `watching`/`tracking`). On Discourse, `regular` still generates notifications (e.g., mentions, replies to own posts), so the promise to “stop receiving notifications” is false for many recipients — they will continue to get some notifications/emails. This is a behavior/docs mismatch introduced by this PR. If the intent is to fully stop per-topic emails, set to `muted` unconditionally; if the intent is to downgrade (watching → tracking → regular), adjust the copy accordingly (e.g., “reduce notifications”). As-is it’s misleading and user-hostile.

https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua.pr_title: Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins

golden_comments.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Flex migration risks right-alignment regression: `margin-left: auto` on `.panel` won’t work with prefixed flex fallbacks (IE10/11, old WebKit) added by the mixins

This change removes `float: right` from `.panel` and relies on flex with `margin-left: auto` to push it to the right (`app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss`: the new `.contents` gains `@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);` and `.panel` gains `margin-left: auto; @include order(3);`). While modern flex supports the auto-margin trick, the newly introduced prefixed displays (`display: -ms-flexbox`, `display: -webkit-box`, etc.) do not consistently support auto margins for alignment (notably IE10/11, and the 2009 `-webkit-box` model). Without complementary packing on the container (`-ms-flex-pack: end;`, `-webkit-box-pack: end;`, and `justify-content: flex-end|space-between`), the panel can remain left-aligned or collapse into the flow in these browsers, a silent behavior change versus the prior `float: right` fallback.

Suggested fix: On `.contents`, add explicit cross-version packing to ensure right alignment across the prefixed implementations, e.g. a `justify-content` mixin that sets `-ms-flex-pack: end;`, `-webkit-box-pack: end;`, and `justify-content: flex-end` (or `space-between` if you need left and right extremes). Alternatively, retain a `float: right` fallback behind a `@supports not (display: flex)` rule for non-modern engines. Document and test the behavior on IE11/old WebKit if those are in your support matrix.

[BLOCKING] `align-items` mixin includes invalid `-ms-align-items` and does not map `baseline` to any supported IE10/11 value

In `app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss`, the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` sets `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and also `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The `-ms-align-items` property does not exist and will be ignored. Additionally, IE10/11’s `-ms-flex-align` accepts `start|end|center|stretch` (no `baseline`). You invoke `@include align-items(center);` in `header.scss` and `@include align-items(baseline);` in `badges.css.scss`. In IE, `baseline` will be ignored, yielding inconsistent alignment across engines. 

Suggested fix: Remove the invalid `-ms-align-items` line. Add a value-normalization layer in the mixin to map unsupported values; e.g., treat `baseline` as `start` for `-ms-flex-align`. Optionally split into `@mixin align-items-center`, etc., or add a `@mixin justify-content`/`align-items` pair that emits correct prefixed properties per value.

[NON-BLOCKING] `order($val)` mixin risks off-by-one across legacy vs modern flexbox (`-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is 1-based; `order` is 0-based)

The new `@mixin order($val)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val;` and `order: $val;`. In the 2009 WebKit flexbox model, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` starts at 1 (the default is 1), whereas modern `order` starts at 0 (default 0). Passing the same `$val` to both can produce different relative orderings across engines (e.g., `order(0)` makes a modern item lead but can collapse to default group 0 vs 1 semantics, and `order(3)` can appear as 3 in modern but as 3rd group starting at 1 in old WebKit). Consider normalizing by emitting `$val + 1` for `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, or constrain accepted inputs to avoid 0 where legacy is in play. Add a comment or unit visual test to prevent regressions.

[NON-BLOCKING] Flex conversion of `.small-action` removed left offset and may cause avatar/text overlap or inconsistent spacing at wide widths

`.small-action` now uses flex and `align-items(center)` while `.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` to `padding: 0 1.5%` and `p` margins were collapsed to `0`. If `.topic-avatar` has no explicit right margin or fixed basis, text can butt up against the avatar. The percentage padding also scales with container width, producing excessive horizontal gutters on very wide screens compared to the prior fixed `4em` left clearance which guaranteed avatar space.

Suggestion: add an explicit gap between flex children (e.g., `column-gap` or a right margin on `.topic-avatar`), and consider a fixed/breakpoint-based left offset for `.small-action-desc` to preserve consistent alignment. Verify on narrow and very wide viewports and RTL locales.

[NON-BLOCKING] `align-items` mixin omits `-moz-box-align`, despite emitting `display: -moz-box` in `flexbox()`/`inline-flex()`

The `@mixin flexbox()` and `@mixin inline-flex()` include `display: -moz-box`/`-moz-inline-box` (2009 syntax), but `@mixin align-items($alignment)` sets only `-webkit-box-align`, not the Firefox counterpart `-moz-box-align`. On engines that still parse `-moz-box`, vertical centering via `@include align-items(center);` won’t apply. If you intend to keep `-moz-box`, add `-moz-box-align: <mapped-value>` in the mixin or drop `-moz-*` fallbacks entirely and rely on unprefixed modern flex + Autoprefixer.

https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua.pr_title: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain

golden_comments.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Potential FrozenError and unintended mutation from using `"." << website_host` in `ends_with?` check

In `website_name`, the else-branch builds the suffix with `"." << website_host` inside `discourse_host.ends_with?(...)`. The `<<` operator mutates its receiver. Using it on a string literal risks a `FrozenError` if frozen string literals are enabled for this file or project (common in modern Ruby configurations), and is generally brittle. It also performs an in-place mutation on a temporary string, which is unnecessary here.

Suggested fix: avoid `<<` with a literal; use `"." + website_host` or string interpolation `".${website_host}"` (Ruby: `"." + website_host` or `".#{website_host}"`) to construct the suffix without mutation:

```rb
discourse_host.end_with?("." + website_host) ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host
# or
suffix = ".#{website_host}"
discourse_host.end_with?(suffix) ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host
```

This is a small change but prevents runtime errors under frozen string literal mode and avoids mutating a string unnecessarily.

[NON-BLOCKING] Unnecessary repeated URI parsing and potential inconsistency; parse once and reuse `path`

`website_name` calls `URI(website.to_s)` up to three separate times (to get `host` and then `path` in the return branches). This is minor but wasteful and risks subtle inconsistency if `website` is mutated between calls. Parse the URI once and reuse both `host` and `path`:

```rb
u = URI.parse(website.to_s) rescue nil
return if u&.host.nil?
website_host = u.host

Also verify that the factory’s `__init__` receives the parsed `flusher_processes` kwarg as intended.

[BLOCKING] Process-type check may be wrong for context-specific processes; `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` can return false for `spawn` context

In `_ensure_processes_alive()` you gate calling `process.kill()` behind `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. When creating processes via a context (`multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`), the returned class is a context-specific subclass that is not guaranteed to be `multiprocessing.Process`. This check can evaluate to `False`, skipping `kill()` on real processes and leaking them after restart attempts. Use a capability check (e.g., `hasattr(process, "kill")`) or check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` (or the context’s own `Process` type) instead. The same pattern appears in `join()` for `process.terminate()`.

[BLOCKING] `flusher_processes` value is not validated; 0 or negative yields `num_processes = 0` and no flusher processes are created

`__init__` computes `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` after setting `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. If a user passes `--flusher-processes=0` (or any non-positive), `self.max_processes` becomes 0 and `self.num_processes` becomes 0, resulting in an empty `process_to_shards_map` and no calls to `_create_process_for_shards()` — the flusher never starts. Please clamp to a minimum of 1 (and optionally enforce an upper bound), and surface invalid values early (e.g., raise on <= 0) to avoid silently disabling flushing.

[NON-BLOCKING] `self.process_restarts` counting is per-process but the MAX is global; unclear policy and potential imbalance

You track restarts per process in `self.process_restarts[process_index]`, but the threshold `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` is global across all processes. This can lead to uneven behavior: a single hot shard can repeatedly hit the cap while others run fine, but the cap logic and error message read as if they applied to the whole flusher. Consider either: (a) a global rolling window across all processes that restarts the whole consumer if aggregate restarts exceed a threshold, or (b) make the limit explicitly per-process and clarify the metric and raised exception accordingly. At minimum, rename and tag metrics to include `process_index`/`shard` to aid diagnosis.

[BLOCKING] Uses non-existent queue APIs (`queue.ShutDown`, `Queue.shutdown`) causing crashes and unshuttable workers

`OrderedQueueWorker.run` catches `queue.ShutDown` (around lines 128 and 145), and `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` (around line 228). Python's standard `queue` module does not define a `ShutDown` exception nor a `Queue.shutdown` method. This will raise `AttributeError`/never be triggered, leading to threads that cannot be cleanly stopped and possibly a hang on shutdown. Use a sentinel item, `queue.Empty` with `get(timeout=...)` + a shutdown flag, or an event to signal worker termination, and do not reference non-existent queue APIs.

`OrderedQueueWorker.run` calls `self.work_queue.get()` with no timeout and only checks `self.shutdown` after it returns. Since there is no sentinel item enqueued on shutdown, workers may block indefinitely on `get()` and ignore `shutdown=True`. Combine a timeout (`get(timeout=...)`) with periodic `shutdown` checks, or push a sentinel to each queue to unblock `get()` and exit cleanly.

[BLOCKING] Unbounded queues create no backpressure and risk OOM; contradicts docstring

`FixedQueuePool` creates each `queue.Queue()` without a `maxsize` (around lines 167-185), which makes them unbounded. The class docstring claims “Natural backpressure when queues fill up,” but with an unbounded `Queue` they never fill up — producers will enqueue indefinitely if downstream is slow, risking unbounded memory growth and process OOM under backlog scenarios. Either set a sensible `maxsize` (and handle `queue.Full`/blocking semantics) or implement explicit backpressure at `submit`.

[BLOCKING] `max_workers=0` leads to ZeroDivisionError in queue index computation

In `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__`, when `mode == "thread-queue-parallel"` the `FixedQueuePool` is constructed with `num_queues=max_workers or 20`. If a caller passes `--max-workers 0` (valid `int`), `max_workers or 20` will coerce to 20 here, which avoids zero — but `uptime_options` exposes this as a generic parallelism knob and nothing prevents 0 in other call sites or future reuse. More critically, `FixedQueuePool.get_queue_for_group` computes `hash(group_key) % self.num_queues`; if `num_queues` is ever 0 (e.g., from a direct call site or a refactor that removes the `or 20` guard), this will raise `ZeroDivisionError` at runtime. Add explicit validation to reject `num_queues <= 0` in `FixedQueuePool.__init__` and to guard `max_workers` in the factory to ensure `>= 1`.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Backup code comparison is case-sensitive; valid uppercase input will be rejected

In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, when validating a backup code you compare the user input with the stored codes using `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` (around the new backup-code branch). The generated codes are lowercased hex via `randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, but the UI encourages an uppercase format (placeholder `"XXXXX-XXXXX"`), and users may type uppercase letters. Without normalizing case, `"ABCDEF"` will not match a stored `"abcdef"`. Normalize the input (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`) before comparison in both the credentials flow and the disable-2FA API. This is a silent auth failure for legitimate users.

[BLOCKING] Backup code comparison does not normalize case/whitespace, causing valid inputs to be rejected

In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the backup code path compares `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` to the stored codes. Users may enter uppercase letters or include whitespace when copying (the UI placeholder is `"XXXXX-XXXXX"`). Without normalizing `.toLowerCase()` and trimming, a valid code like `"ABCD E-F0123"` will fail. Normalize the provided code (trim, remove dashes/whitespace, and lower-case) before lookup. Apply the same normalization in the NextAuth `authorize` backup-code branch to keep behavior consistent.

[BLOCKING] Backup code consumption is not atomic; concurrent use can authorize twice (race condition)

In the NextAuth `authorize` flow, when a backup code matches you perform `backupCodes[index] = null` in memory and then `await prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes)) } })`. There is no atomic check-and-consume at the database level. Two concurrent requests with the same valid code can both read the same pre-update array, both see the code present, and both authorize before either update lands — enabling a single-use code to be used multiple times under load or by a replay. Fix by making consumption atomic (e.g., include the current encrypted value in a conditional update, or store hashed codes each with a "used" flag and mark-used via a transaction that verifies the code was unused).

[NON-BLOCKING] Backup codes are stored symmetrically encrypted, not hashed — increases blast radius if key/user row is compromised

The new `backupCodes` are persisted as a JSON array encrypted with `symmetricEncrypt`. Anyone with DB access plus the encryption key (already required elsewhere in the app) can decrypt all codes; a user-row exfiltration post-key exposure would reveal still-valid codes. Best practice is to store one-way hashes (e.g., salted with per-user/pepper) and verify via constant-time compare, marking consumed atomically. Consider migrating to hashed codes with an atomic consume (`usedAt`/`revoked` flag or code deletion) to reduce risk. This is an improvement suggestion, not a merge blocker, but the current design materially raises recovery-code sensitivity.
