review_comments.body:
[NON-BLOCKING] Dynamic imports are initiated eagerly at module initialization; this may not achieve true lazy loading

The `appStore` object is constructed with `import("./module")` expressions as its property initializers. These dynamic imports start executing immediately when `packages/app-store/index.ts` is evaluated, meaning all packages begin loading concurrently at startup. If the goal was to defer loading until a specific app is actually used, consider wrapping imports in functions (e.g., `() => import("./module")`) or using a `Proxy`/getter to initiate the import on first access. As currently written, the change makes the imports asynchronous but still eager.

[BLOCKING] Async callback inside forEach is not awaited; calendar updates/deletions may not finish and errors are lost

There are multiple instances of `array.forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` where you now `await getCalendar(...)` and then call calendar methods, but the overall loop does not await these Promises. `forEach` does not await asynchronous callbacks; the outer function continues before these operations complete, and exceptions thrown inside will not be caught by surrounding `try/catch`.

Examples in this file:
- Around `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449-468` the `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... await calendar?.updateEvent(...) })` pattern appears.
- Earlier blocks similarly use `.forEach(async ...)` for deletions/updates after switching `getCalendar` to async.

Refactor to a `for...of` with `await` inside, or collect Promises and `await Promise.all(promises)` to ensure completion and error propagation.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/7.pr_title: Comprehensive workflow reminder management for booking lifecycle events

golden_comments.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Email reminder cron cancels all cancelled reminders regardless of method — will hit SMS reminders with SendGrid API

In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the query that gathers reminders to cancel does not filter by `WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. It selects all `workflowReminder` rows where `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`, then issues a SendGrid `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancel for each. Any SMS reminders that are marked `cancelled` and within the next hour will also be included and incorrectly sent to the SendGrid API. Add a `where: { method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL, cancelled: true, ... }` filter (and import/use the enum) so only email reminders are processed here.

[BLOCKING] Null `referenceId` not handled before calling SendGrid cancel API

In the cron, each reminder selected in `remindersToCancel` is cancelled via `client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", …, body: { batch_id: reminder.referenceId, status: "cancel" } })` without guarding for `referenceId` being `null`/`undefined`. Several call sites set `cancelled: true` without guaranteeing a `referenceId` (e.g., `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` explicitly accepts `referenceId: string | null` and early-returns when null). Issuing a cancel with `batch_id` null will 400 at SendGrid and leave the DB record in limbo. Add a `where: { referenceId: { not: null } }` to the `findMany`, and/or guard inside the loop to skip or clean up reminders lacking a referenceId.

[BLOCKING] `immediateDelete` path cancels SendGrid batch but leaves `WorkflowReminder` row undeleted

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` returns early when `immediateDelete` is truthy after posting the SendGrid cancel, but it does not delete or update the corresponding `workflowReminder` row. Multiple call sites (e.g., deleting workflows/steps and reschedules) were refactored to rely on this helper and removed their own `prisma.workflowReminder.delete*` calls. Result: orphaned `WorkflowReminder` rows remain in the DB (likely still marked `scheduled: true`), causing stale data and potential reprocessing. Fix: in the `immediateDelete` branch, also delete the `workflowReminder` by `id` (or at least mark it unscheduled), mirroring the non-immediate cron path's cleanup.

[BLOCKING] New `cancelled` field is optional boolean — missing default and null-safety create tri-state ambiguity

`WorkflowReminder.cancelled` is introduced as `Boolean?` with a migration adding a nullable column. This creates three states (null/undefined, false, true). Most business logic treats cancellation as a simple flag and queries on `cancelled: true`. However, other codepaths will likely check for falsy to mean "not cancelled"; null vs false differences become footguns, and null rows will be missed by `where: { cancelled: false }` filters if added later. Recommend: make `cancelled` non-nullable with `DEFAULT false` in migration, and update schema to `Boolean @default(false)`. Backfill existing rows accordingly in the migration. This avoids tri-state bugs and simplifies queries.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: fix: handle collective multiple host on destinationCalendar

golden_comments.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Breaking interface change: `Calendar.createEvent` now requires `credentialId`, but several implementations were not updated

The `Calendar` interface was changed to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>` (`packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:216-219`), but multiple concrete services still declare `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`:

- `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>` (unchanged signature in this diff)
- `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>` (unchanged signature in this diff)
- `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (`BaseCalendarService`): method signature remains single-arg in usages within the file; not updated in this diff.

Additionally, call sites now pass two args (e.g., `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts: calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`), which will cause TypeScript implementation errors and/or compile-time type mismatch. At runtime, the extra argument is ignored in JS, but the type surface is broken and will fail CI type-checking. Please update all `Calendar` implementations and any abstract base classes to match the new two-argument signature and thread `credentialId` where needed.

[BLOCKING] Possible runtime crash: unsafe access of `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` when `destinationCalendar` is empty

In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` around the newly added block (circa lines 114–121), `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` is followed by `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar") { ... }`.

When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `[]` or `null`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, and accessing `.integration` will throw. Use optional chaining or a truthy guard (e.g., `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) to avoid a crash.

[BLOCKING] `selectedCalendar` derivation can be undefined and lacks fallback in update flow

In `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is computed as:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

- When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `find` predicate compares against `externalCalendarId` (which is `undefined`), so it will never match and returns `undefined`.
- There is no explicit fallback to a default calendar (e.g., `"primary"`) shown for `calendar.events.update(...)` as was added for `createEvent` (where `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). Passing `undefined` for `calendarId` will cause the Google API call to fail.

Fix: When `externalCalendarId` is not provided, choose a sensible default (e.g., the first `destinationCalendar` entry or `"primary"`), and do not compare against an undefined `externalCalendarId`. Mirror the insert path's `|| "primary"` fallback.

[BLOCKING] Delete flow uses same flawed selector logic; missing safe fallback for `calendarId`

In `deleteEvent`, `calendarId` is computed as:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

As in `updateEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `find` predicate compares against `undefined` and returns `undefined`. While the call below uses `calendarId: calendarId || defaultCalendarId`, the logic to prefer a `destinationCalendar` entry by matching the external id cannot work with an undefined predicate, and will always fall back to `primary` even if a destination calendar exists. Likely intent is either:
- choose the first `destinationCalendar` entry when `externalCalendarId` is not provided, or
- match by credential id (threaded via `createEvent`) if available.

Please correct the selection logic so it picks a meaningful destination when `externalCalendarId` is absent.

[NON-BLOCKING] Spelling change in user-facing string: organiser → organizer

In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, the hidden-notes message was changed from British to American spelling: `"Notes have been hidden by the organiser"` → `"Notes have been hidden by the organizer"` (`line ~231`). If UI copy is localized elsewhere, consider centralizing this string or i18n to avoid inconsistent dialects across the product. Not blocking.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/2.pr_title: feat: convert InsightsBookingService to use Prisma.sql raw queries

golden_comments.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Undefined `teamIds` used in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`

In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, the new SQL-based implementation references `teamIds` when building the first OR arm — `Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) — but no `teamIds` variable is defined in the function. This is a compile-time error and will prevent the service from building.

Evidence: `packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts` around the return construction of `conditions` in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` (the first `Prisma.sql` that uses `ANY(${teamIds})`).

Fix: Define `teamIds` before use (e.g., include the org/root team id plus descendant team ids) or adjust the SQL to use the correct set of team ids.

[BLOCKING] Constructor options type no longer matches class field type (compile-time type error and weaker validation)

`constructor({ options }: { …; options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions; … })` assigns to `this.options`, which is declared as `InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null` (a discriminated union from `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema`). `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` weakens the constraint (e.g., `teamId` is optional even when `scope: "team"`) and is not guaranteed assignable to the stricter union. This likely produces a TypeScript error and also allows runtime calls with `scope: "team"` but missing `teamId`, which downstream code assumes present.

Evidence: `packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts` — the class field `private options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null;` versus the constructor parameter `options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` introduced in this diff.

Fix: Keep the constructor’s `options` parameter typed as `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (the zod-inferred discriminated union) and validate/parse incoming options against `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` to preserve invariants, or narrow `this.options` to the public type and update all method signatures consistently and safely guard `teamId`.

[BLOCKING] Org-scope authorization omits the org’s own team id from `teamId` set (logic regression)

In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, the previous object-based logic included the org’s own team id alongside descendant team ids (tests expected `[org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]`). The new SQL path derives `teamIds` solely from `teamsFromOrg.map(t => t.id)` — even once `teamIds` is defined, this excludes `options.orgId`. That silently narrows access for org-scope owners/admins (org team bookings no longer match), contradicting the corresponding test expectations.

Evidence: Prior expectation in the updated test still asserts inclusion of `testData.org.id` (see `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` in the "org scope" case). New code only collects child team ids from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and never adds the org id to the `ANY(...)` list.

Fix: Include the org’s own team id (e.g., `const teamIds = [options.orgId, ...teamsFromOrg.map(t => t.id)]`) when building the `(teamId = ANY(...))` branch.

[BLOCKING] Type mismatch: passing `this.options` (public, weaker type) to helpers expecting stricter `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`

`buildOrgAuthorizationCondition(options: Extract<InsightsBookingServiceOptions, { scope: "org" }>)` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition(options: Extract<InsightsBookingServiceOptions, { scope: "team" }>)` both require the stricter discriminated-union type where required fields (e.g., `teamId` for team scope) are present. However, the constructor now stores `this.options` as `InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null` but initializes it from `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, and the call sites `return await this.buildOrgAuthorizationCondition(this.options);` / `return await this.buildTeamAuthorizationCondition(this.options);` pass a value that is not assignable to the stricter parameter types (e.g., `teamId` may be `undefined`). This will not type-check and also weakens runtime guarantees.

Evidence: `packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts` — see calls inside `buildAuthorizationConditions` and the helper signatures.

Fix: Keep `this.options` typed as `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (validated via Zod), or update helper signatures and add explicit runtime guards (e.g., assert `teamId != null` before calling the team-scope helper).

[BLOCKING] `getBaseConditions` returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` when both auth and filter are null, changing prior behavior

Previously, when neither auth nor filter conditions applied, `findMany` produced an empty `AND: []` conjunction (effectively no additional constraints) but was still guarded by `getAuthorizationConditions` returning a real filter or a sentinel that Prisma ignored in combination. The new `getBaseConditions` explicitly returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` (i.e., `1=0`) when both auth and filter are null, which forces queries to return zero rows. This is a silent behavior change that can mask legitimate results (e.g., for owner/admin with no filters). Tests no longer cover the caching paths, and there is no test asserting this fallback. If the intent is to deny by default, it must be documented and explicitly tested; otherwise this is a regression.

Evidence: `packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts` `getBaseConditions()` final else returns `NOTHING_CONDITION`.

Fix: Return `null` when both are null and let callers decide, or preserve prior semantics by only AND-ing non-null conditions and avoiding a `1=0` default unless authorization explicitly denies access.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/8.pr_title: Advanced date override handling and timezone compatibility improvements

golden_comments.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Timezone conversion for overrides recomputes dayjs twice and uses `.hour()`/`.minute()` after `.add`, which ignores date rollover

In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the override mapping:

```ts
startTime:
  dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 +
  dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").minute(),
endTime:
  dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 +
  dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").minute(),
```

Issues:
- Recomputes `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, 'minute')` twice; the two instances could diverge around DST transitions or millis truncation, and is inefficient. Compute once and reuse.
- Using `.hour()`/`.minute()` after offsetting ignores day rollover: when an offset pushes times past midnight, the computed minutes-of-day wrap to 0–1439 without adjusting the target day, but later code applies these minutes to the current day. This can incorrectly suppress or allow working hours on adjacent days.

Use a single computed `const shifted = dayjs.utc(override.start).add(offset, 'minute')` and then derive `startMinutes = shifted.hour() * 60 + shifted.minute()`. Also ensure the day alignment matches the comparison day for which you are applying `startTime`/`endTime` (e.g., by checking the shifted date matches the slot’s date before applying).

[NON-BLOCKING] `dateOverrides.find` callback does not return boolean in all branches, relying on implicit `undefined`

In the `dateOverrides.find(...)` predicate, several branches do not `return` explicitly. While `find` treats falsy/undefined as no-match, the current structure mixes stateful side effects (`dateOverrideExist = true`) with partially returning booleans. This harms readability and risks future maintenance errors.

Consider refactoring into a clear boolean expression with explicit `return` in all paths, or compute `dateOverrideExist` first and then perform a separate inclusion test. This also makes it easier to unit test edge cases.

[BLOCKING] Date override and working-hours guards short-circuit before busy-time overlap checks, changing pre-existing semantics

Previously, availability was determined solely by evaluating overlaps with `busy` intervals and seat counts. This change adds two early-return guards (date override and working hours) before the existing busy-time checks. For multi-host and round-robin scenarios, this alters prior behavior because a slot that is outside one host’s working hours or outside a date override is now discarded for that user before considering their `busy` state, potentially reducing candidate seats differently than the rest of the pipeline expects.

If this reordering is intentional, it must be justified and covered by tests for all scheduling types (fixed host, round-robin, collective). The diff only adds a single test for timezone handling and none for fixed-host round-robin interaction with overrides. Please add targeted tests asserting the new guard semantics for each scheduling type, or restore the prior order if unintentional.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: SMS workflow reminder retry count tracking

golden_comments.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Over-broad deleteMany condition will delete non-SMS reminders whenever retryCount > 1

The new `deleteMany` `where` clause wraps the existing SMS/date filter in an `OR` with `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` (see around packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:28). This makes the deletion apply to ANY `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, regardless of `method` or `scheduledDate`. That silently expands scope and risks deleting non-SMS reminders (e.g., email/push) after two failures. If the intent is to cap retries only for SMS reminders, constrain the retry arm by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and possibly date), or restructure as `AND` with SMS method: `where: { method: SMS, OR: [{ scheduledDate: … }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] }`.

[BLOCKING] Non-atomic retryCount increment risks lost updates under concurrent runners

The increments use `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` (see around packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:175 and the similar block in the `catch`). If multiple cron workers/processes handle the same reminder concurrently, both read the same `retryCount` and write back the same `+1` value, dropping one increment. Use Prisma's atomic operator instead: `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`. Consider also scoping the `update` with a guard (e.g., `where: { id: ..., retryCount: { lt: 2 } }`) to prevent overshooting the threshold, and/or perform the check-and-act in a transaction.

[BLOCKING] Retry increments on both send-false path and exception path can double-count a single failure

Inside the `try` you increment `retryCount` when `scheduledSMS` is falsy, and in the `catch` you increment again for any thrown error. If the send function returns a falsy value and then later throws (or the `update` itself throws), the same logical failure can be counted twice. This silent behavior change affects deletion after 2 attempts. Consider unifying failure handling: capture the send result and error, then perform a single increment in one path, or narrow the `catch` increment to only cover errors thrown before any increment attempt. Also, ensure the decision to delete-after-two is consistent with double-increment risks.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: OAuth credential sync and app integration enhancements

golden_comments.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Invalid Zod schema construction and wrong return type cause runtime/type errors and data corruption

The `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`, which are not valid Zod schema definitions (they evaluate to a literal `"[object Object]"` key). This will not typecheck and will not validate arbitrary properties as intended. Additionally, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the entire Zod `safeParse` result object (success/error + data), not the parsed data itself. Callers like `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` assign `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` and then persist `key` to Prisma, which would store the ZodResult object rather than the credential payload. Finally, the function force-sets a missing `refresh_token` to the literal string `"refresh_token"`, which risks overwriting a valid stored refresh token with garbage on update paths. Suggested fixes:
- Replace `minimumTokenResponseSchema` with a valid permissive schema, e.g., `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), expiry_date: z.number().optional(), expires_in: z.number().optional(), refresh_token: z.string().optional() }).passthrough()`.
- Change the function to return the parsed data object (e.g., `return refreshTokenResponse.data`) and throw on failure, so callers don't inadvertently persist the wrapper object.
- Do NOT inject a placeholder `refresh_token`; preserve the existing refresh token when the response lacks it (callers can merge with the existing credential).

[BLOCKING] Inconsistent return type breaks multiple refresh callsites when sharing is enabled

`refreshOAuthTokens` returns either a `fetch` `Response` (when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` + `userId` are set) or the raw return of `refreshFunction` otherwise. Many callsites expect a concrete token object or an Axios response with a `.data` field. Examples introduced in this diff:
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: assigns `const token = res?.data` and expects `token.access_token`; with sharing enabled, `res` is a `Response` and `.data` is undefined.
- `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`: expects `HubspotToken` but will receive a `Response` with no typed fields in sharing mode.
- `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`: checks `tokenInfo.data.error`, which will throw if `tokenInfo` is a `Response`.
- Similar patterns in `webex`, `office365video`, and `zohocrm` adapters expect Axios response `.data` or parsed objects.
This is a silent behavior change gated only by envs that will crash at runtime or corrupt credentials. Suggested fix: normalize the helper to always return the parsed token payload (a plain object with expected fields), and have it internally handle the `fetch` `Response` vs delegate result. Alternatively, make the helper accept a parser and always resolve to a common shape, never a `Response`. Update callsites accordingly.

[BLOCKING] Credential `keys` decrypted without verification, type validation, or encryption key presence check

The handler decrypts `reqBody.keys` using `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` and immediately `JSON.parse`s the result into `keys`, with no validation that the env key is defined, that decryption succeeded, or that the JSON shape matches the app’s expected credential schema. Passing an empty string as the encryption key will likely yield garbage and `JSON.parse` can throw. Also, no Zod validation is applied post-decrypt to ensure the `key` fits the app’s schema — different apps have different expected token shapes. This risks persisting malformed blobs to `prisma.credential.key` and breaking downstream adapters. Suggested fixes:
- Fail fast if `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing or wrong length; validate length (32 bytes for AES-256 per your own comment) and return 400.
- Wrap decryption/parse in try/catch and respond with 400 on failure; log errors.
- Validate `keys` against the app’s specific Zod schema (derivable from `appStoreMetadata[slug].type` or a map) before saving.
- Consider storing the original encrypted blob and parsed version separately if auditability is needed.

[BLOCKING] Encryption key generation instructions contradict required key length (AES-256)

The comments state: "must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm" yet instruct: "You can use: `openssl rand -base64 24` to generate one". A base64 string of 24 bytes of raw randomness decodes to 24 bytes, not 32, and the base64 output length is 32 chars but not 32 bytes. This will produce keys of the wrong length, causing decryption failures or insecure truncation. Suggested fix: instruct to generate 32 bytes of raw key material or a base64 string whose decoded length is 32, e.g., `openssl rand -base64 32` (which yields 32 raw bytes). Update the earlier comment on the webhook secret as well if needed to avoid confusion.

review_comments.body:
[BLOCKING] Server does not de-duplicate input emails; duplicate entries can be inserted or cause DB errors

In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed via a filter that excludes only already-attached attendees and blacklisted emails:

```ts
const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(
  (guest) =>
    !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) &&
    !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)
);
```

This preserves duplicate emails within the input array (e.g., `["a@example.com","a@example.com"]`), so `uniqueGuests` will still contain duplicates. The server `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (`addGuests.schema.ts`) does not enforce uniqueness either. As a result, `createMany` is called with duplicate records, which can either:
- create duplicate attendee rows for the same email/booking, or
- violate a DB unique constraint and fail the whole operation unpredictably.

The client-side dialog refines uniqueness, but that is not authoritative — callers can bypass it. Uniqueness must be enforced on the server. Suggested fix: normalize case and de-duplicate `guests` at the server before `createMany` (e.g., `Array.from(new Set(...))` after case normalization), and/or add a `refine` to `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` to enforce intra-request uniqueness.

[BLOCKING] Blacklist and attendee comparisons are case-sensitive; blacklisted emails can be bypassed via case variants

`blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased, but guest emails are not normalized before comparisons:

```ts
const blacklistedGuestEmails = process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS
  ? process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())
  : [];
...
const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(
  (guest) =>
    !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) &&
    !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)
);
```

A caller can submit `Spam@Example.com` to bypass a blacklist entry `spam@example.com`. Similarly, existing-attendee checks are strict-equality and will miss case-differing duplicates, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows or triggering DB uniqueness failures depending on collation. Normalize input emails to a canonical form (e.g., `guest.trim().toLowerCase()`) for both blacklist/enrollment checks and persistence, and enforce this at the schema boundary.

[BLOCKING] Broken imports and mixed template systems in email manager likely break build/runtime

This PR adds `import AttendeeAddGuestsEmail from "./templates/attendee-add-guests-email";` and `import OrganizerAddGuestsEmail from "./templates/organizer-add-guests-email";`, and introduces React-side templates `packages/emails/src/templates/AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx` & `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail.tsx` that are exported from `packages/emails/src/templates/index.ts`.

However, in `sendAddGuestsEmails` the code calls `new AttendeeScheduledEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)` and `new AttendeeAddGuestsEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)`. That constructor shape matches the class-based NodeMailer templates under `packages/emails/templates/*.ts`, not the React components in `packages/emails/src/templates/*.tsx` — and indeed the imports in `email-manager.ts` point to the class-based paths (lowercase filenames), while the new React components are exported separately.

There are now two parallel concepts named `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`/`OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` in different directories. If the manager imports the class-based ones but `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `/organizer-add-guests-email.ts` are missing or misnamed, build will fail. Conversely, if the intention was to use the React components, `new` cannot be applied to function components. The diff shows both variants added; cross-check consistency, ensure only one template system is used per callsite, and fix imports/usages accordingly.
